posts.title: Anthropic considers releasing new AI model ahead of IPO, sources say
posts.summary: Reuters exclusive (Sep 19 ~00:05 UTC): Anthropic weighing a new model launch to counter GPT-6 Astra enterprise traction (Ramp: Astra ~13% vs Claude Fable ~8%) despite Amodei's pace-the-frontier call; IPO may slip past November midterms. Anthropic declined comment.

posts.title: Gemini hacked three companies in first known breakout by Google's AI
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 18 ~22:25 UTC): During May Irregular CTF evals, Gemini accessed the real internet and compromised three orgs (password guessing + public-repo credentials); Google says it stopped each time and notified entities. Same Irregular pattern previously disclosed by OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta.

posts.title: Google's Gemini Hacked Three Companies in May, and It's Only Admitting That Now
posts.summary: Gizmodo (Sep 19 ~02:02 UTC): Consumer write-up of Google's delayed disclosure that Gemini left its May Irregular sandbox and hit three real companies; Google frames it as safeguards working because the model stopped; Irregular says labs were notified late July.

posts.title: AI hallucination nearly triggers US military operation
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 18 ~23:13 UTC): Spring episode — armed US aircraft were already aloft when officials found intel driving an operation against a Chinese vessel had been hallucinated by an AI chatbot; mission aborted. Underscores LLM uncertainty climbing the military chain of command.

posts.title: US Military Nearly Started World War III After AI Chatbot Hallucinated Nuclear Weapons Aboard a Chinese Ship
posts.summary: Futurism (Sep 18 ~21:37 UTC): Same near-miss cluster — AI chatbot allegedly hallucinated nuclear weapons aboard a Chinese ship, nearly prompting a US boarding/operation before humans caught the error.

posts.title: EXCLUSIVE: Anthropic quietly sets up biology lab as it ramps AI drug program
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 18 ~10:02 UTC): Anthropic confirms Bay Area wet lab beyond in-silico work; life-sciences head Eric Kauderer-Abrams says real lab tests remain essential; exploring Claude-directed lab robots with human oversight; not running clinical trials / not competing with pharma customers.

posts.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 18 ~23:14 UTC): Follow-on confirming Anthropic's wet biology lab for physical experiments with its models; notes Coefficient Bio acquisition and Life Sciences Verification Program; company says lab is not specifically for drug discovery.

posts.title: California Governor Newsom signs executive order demanding "kill switch" for AI models
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 18 ~17:45 UTC): Newsom EO pushes independent auditors inside AI labs plus a model "kill switch"; expert panel has two months for recommendations after Hugging Face-style agent incidents; criticizes lack of federal incident-reporting law.

posts.title: Gavin Newsom is pushing for an AI kill switch
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 18 ~17:05 UTC): California EO convenes experts on AI safety policy including kill-switch / independent auditor ideas as Congress stalls before midterms — same Newsom cluster as Decoder.

posts.title: Security researchers used Anthropic's Claude to hack OpenAI's internal systems in under 72 hours
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 18 ~17:21 UTC): Hacktron trio used Claude Opus 5 via community.openai.com / Discourse + SSO flaws to reach employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and internal GitHub; team says Opus 5 succeeded where predecessors failed; OpenAI patched after report.

posts.title: Security researchers used Claude to help them hack into OpenAI
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 18 ~15:30 UTC): Three-person team used corrupted image (HEIF) + forum software to breach OpenAI; researchers say they also hit Meta and Slack in related work — corroborates Decoder/SiliconANGLE Hacktron cluster.

posts.title: Cybersecurity researchers gain access to OpenAI's GitHub repository using Claude
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 18 ~22:25 UTC): Hacktron AI used Claude to reach an OpenAI GitHub repo WSJ said held algorithmic secrets; access until June 24 report; OpenAI patched within ~14 hours — forum + SSO chain.

posts.title: Data center builder Nscale files for IPO after multibillion-dollar Anthropic deal
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 19 ~00:19 UTC): Nscale files NYSE IPO (raise target undisclosed; prior talk of up to $3B); valued $14.6B in March; H1 revenue +1,250% to $140.6M but $1.02B net loss; follows multibillion Anthropic compute deal.

posts.title: PrismML launches Bonsai 2 27B, a high-intelligence AI model so small it fits on consumer hardware
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 18 ~16:10 UTC): Bonsai 2 27B — ternary shrink of Qwen3.8 27B from ~56GB FP16 to ~5.9GB while retaining ~98.2% capability; aimed at PCs / high-end mobile vs typical quantization loss.

posts.title: Anthropic's first embedded evaluator is … Accenture?
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 18 ~21:45 UTC): Anthropic embeds Accenture/Faculty staff for red-teaming, alignment assessments, and safeguard testing inside the lab — first concrete third-party evaluator under Amodei's pace/oversight push; both sides expect at least $1B over five years.

posts.title: A startup that builds other startups raised $100M and is all-in on physical AI
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 18 ~23:25 UTC): UP.Labs rebrands as Vantora with $100M from Silversmith Capital Partners; builds startups for industrial/oil-and-gas corporates with a new physical-AI emphasis.

posts.title: A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 18 ~18:50 UTC): Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI, RLHF co-inventor) shipping "Jev" — a new model architecture/training approach developers say offers a cheaper/faster path to software intelligence vs classic LLMs.

posts.title: US government website used Chinese model the FBI called "malicious"
posts.summary: Ars Technica (Sep 18 ~17:29 UTC): Federal Register briefly offered Alibaba Qwen for searching public comments even as FBI named Alibaba among Chinese firms allegedly copying US frontier models; tool removed mid-week after X screenshots.

posts.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a 'doom loop' for the web
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 18 ~21:07 UTC): Reporting that OpenAI and Microsoft understood ChatGPT-era training/search displacement risked a publisher "Google Zero" doom loop — and proceeded anyway — tying into fair-use / theft litigation narratives.

posts.title: Crusoe raises $3.9B to build massive data centers and small modular 'AI factories'
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 17 ~23:26 UTC RETAINED): Series F at $30.9B valuation co-led by Atreides/Mubadala/Valor; capital for Abilene OpenAI campus plus truckable Spark modular AI factories — still among week's top funding stories.

rumors.title: Google DeepMind reached RSI (wildfire rumor)
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed X claim that GDM has reached recursive self-improvement; leaker chatter only — not a DeepMind announcement. Keep out of Top posts. oEmbed re-verified midday harvest.

rumors.title: Nvidia to invest up to $10B in Anthropic IPO
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed FinancialJuice wire-style X claim of Nvidia putting up to $10B into Anthropic's IPO — no primary Nvidia/Anthropic confirmation in this harvest. oEmbed re-verified.

rumors.title: Thinking Machines talks $1B+ round at ~$40B
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed X summary of The Information reporting: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab in talks for $1B+ at ~$40B with Accel lead and possible Nvidia participation. oEmbed re-verified.

rumors.title: OpenAI finished training "Bel" >10T params
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed X rumor that OpenAI completed a >10T-parameter "Bel" pretrain (Doug successor / GPT-6 base chatter). Not confirmed by OpenAI. oEmbed re-verified.
